newsitem.title: GERMANY: Treuhand successor says privatisation difficult.
newsitem.headline: Treuhand successor says privatisation difficult.

text.p: The successor to Germany's Treuhand privatisation agency, the BvS, said on Wednesday privatisation of former east German companies was proving more difficult than expected.
But the agency's management said in an interim report after 20 months of work that it still hoped to complete its task by the end of 1998 as originally planned.
The report said the biggest problem had been the shipyards on the Baltic coast but it ruled out long-term subsidies to the yards.
Most of the privatised firms had since become competitive or were not far from it, it said.
Two of its most notable successes were the sale of the Buna/Leuna refineries and rail car maker Deutsche Waggonbau AG.
Since the beginning of 1995, the BvS has forged agreements securing 18,000 jobs and investments totalling 6.3 billion marks ($4.2 billion).
Finance Minister Theo Waigel said in a statement he was pleased the BvS had made no claim on federal funds during 1995 and was unlikely to do so in 1996 or 1997.
